critical_code_review_comments: server.py Insurance payout rate: backend _insurance_derive treats payoutRate as a fraction (expected = premium * rate) while the frontend EntryDrawer stores rate as % (0-100). The form's payoutRate state is initialized as row.payoutRate*100 and then submitted as +form.payoutRate (i.e., in %). Bug: on Save, the number posted is percent (e.g., 10) so expectedPayout becomes premium*10 = 10x the intended amount. Only reason baseline is unaffected is that no UI-created insurance entries exist. Fix: divide by 100 in Insurance.js save() before POST, or normalize server-side. My test bypassed this by posting rate=0.1 directly.

No API to DELETE a Payment record — cleanup after an over-cap test payment required direct Mongo access + a no-op scheme PUT to force recompute_lead. Consider exposing DELETE /payments/{receiptNumber} (owner-only) for corrections.

server.py GET /leads/{id} does not include commercialTotals in the response (frontend derives them via /360). Ensure client code consistently uses /360 endpoint for payable/outstanding calculations to avoid drift.

Finance.js FinanceReceiptModal 'files' prop is populated via view=pending; that's fine, but the modal is not re-fetching after a successful save inside the same session (the parent re-fetches allFiles via a useEffect on `receipt` which flips false), so a second receipt in the same open would show stale outstanding. Minor UX polish.

Claims.js: outstandingRows filter uses `> 0.01` — good; but on the /claims list backend does not send `component` label when the claim doc exists only from a scheme (i.e., no prior settle). Confirm the dropdown option text 'r.component' is populated by the backend list for scheme-derived rows (my backend test hit the claims list and found the row; passed).
